digest.component_or_area: plan review vocabulary and detector system
propositions: The rebar plan vocabulary uses two separate headings, Success Criteria and Acceptance Criteria, that apply identical semantic rules and are treated as one concept by every live gate, making the split vestigial and harmful to checklist counting and operator-attest tagging.

Success Criteria items are conventionally written as plain bullets and do not count toward the P1 blocking floor under _count_ac_items, cannot carry the [operator-attested] tag, and are not individually checkable, creating functional gaps between the two heading types.

Collapsing Success Criteria into Acceptance Criteria across detector regexes, reviewer prompts, routing indices, guides, generated docs, eval specs, test corpus, and 106 stored tickets requires a phased expand-contract migration to avoid creating an un-reviewable state.

Four acceptance criteria initially conflicted with the epic's own scope or child story requirements (AC1 with excluded files, AC4 with runtime-computed set cardinality, AC5 with generated artifact mechanics, and unowned completion.py scope) and required amendment via stale-material re-review.

The migration must exclude the dod_uncertifiable vocabulary in three verifier files and plan_review_T2.md (pilot metrics), O-RAN-SC vendor references, and frozen test fixtures from the collapse scope.

Post-implementation audits found zero remaining Success Criteria headings across 106 migrated tickets and two reintroduced epics, with only eight backticked prose mentions correctly preserved, confirming full vocabulary collapse.
